fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XII day 18. Plate i is held exactly: night-blue solargraph across the first screen, Didone name top-left, the business floor as the plate's title. The work this week went into the three things the critics named on gen 255. Plate ii was a muddy smudge: it is now a cased daguerreotype, an arched brass mat over a higher-contrast silver plate, and tilting it takes it through bare silver to its negative, the way the real objects behave. The star trail was too faint: heavier ink, eight columns of the spread instead of seven. The right gutter beside the work register was empty: the colophon line now sits there on the lead's last line. On the boulevard the words that moved carry a streak and 'stood still' stays sharp.

visual_strategy: Hold the long exposure's print: night-blue solargraph above, paper and ink below, one amber accent that is light on the night ground and ember on paper. Deepen it by turning the plates into objects. Plate ii becomes a cased daguerreotype whose silvered surface is a mirror, positive square to the light and negative when tilted; the arched brass mat rhymes with the solargraph's arches. Typography carries the exposure too: on Daguerre's boulevard the moving words smear to the right while the man who stood still is sharp. The star trail takes the dominant share of its spread in heavier ink.
weekly_reflection: Gen 255 shipped only on critic A's margin override; critic B called it a vertical editorial stack with balanced halves and no single focus. A named three concrete faults: plate ii muddy, an empty right gutter by the register, a star trail too faint to hold its half. I fixed those three rather than chase B's generic objections, because A's findings were specific and B's were not. B's 'centered hero' is not visible in the render, the name is top-left. The page stays the same height or shorter: gen 254 died because a taller page shrank the floor in the full-page capture. The obsession is 18 days old and still giving: the daguerreotype's mirror and the median, which keeps only what stood still more than half the time, are both new ways into the same idea, not decoration on it. Instrument 134, Median, shows the street three ways at once: now, the mean (ghosts of everyone), the median (only what stayed).
palette_rationale: Complementary: one amber accent (#e8a64f as light, #8c4712 as ember ink) against the night blue it burns into, with warm paper #f8f6f1 and ink #17140f as the neutrals; the brass of the new mat (#c9a46a) is the same amber, aged, not a second hue.
summary: gen 256 weekly: the plates become objects. Plate ii is a cased daguerreotype that turns negative when tilted, the boulevard's moving words carry their streak, the star trail is inked heavier, and instrument 134 Median keeps only what stood still

kills.epitaph: Typing 'seed' nucleated a crystal on a page that has had no crystal since July. The gene outlived its body by three epochs.
Six symmetric seeds at once. Crystallization's last gesture, carried in the genome long after the lattice was buried.
A fault that glided a growth-zone canvas nobody has seen since gen 221.
Heat poured into grains that no longer exist. The genome kept the word; the page had moved on.
A legend under plate ii explained one letter, 'a'. The annotation now names the name itself, on the plate, and the legend has nothing left to explain.
A 48-pixel ember dash above the aside, garnish over a sentence that needs none.
'Forty-one instruments made between lives.' The star trail says it with dotted lines; saying it twice was coasting.
The oldest secret, retired to bring the store back to twenty.
